source: CLREQ — Requirements for Chinese Text Layout, W3C DNOTE 2026-11-04 (Group Note Draft, NOT a Recommendation); fetched 2026-11-15 via /TR/2026/DNOTE-clreq-20261104/. Status: draft; clause 6.1.1 explicitly says 'Prohibition rules for line start and line end are styling issues. The user agent can choose or customize the rules'.
read_scope: sections 6.1, 6.1.1, 6.1.2, 6.1.3, 6.2, 6.3 (fulltext of those sections) + appendix punctuation tables; NOT a full compliance audit and NOT a claim that browsers implement every rule.
environment_note: This fixture is rendered in headless Chrome 157 (Blink). CSS values are declared in fixture.html; whether Blink actually applies each specific 禁则 to every CJK punctuation was NOT pixel-verified here. 'css_implemented' means: a standard CSS property is the correct mechanism and is set in the fixture. 'untested' means: no faithful CSS-only mechanism, so behavior is deliberately not asserted.

rules.clreqLocator: §6.1.1 (prohibition-rules-basic): pause/stop punctuation (顿号、逗号、句号、冒号、分号、叹号、问号), closing quotes/brackets/angle brackets, connector marks, interpuncts, solidi should NOT appear at line start; 'This is the most recommended method'
rules.cssProperty: line-break: strict (CSS Text Module Level 3) + word-break: normal
rules.note: line-break:strict is the closest standard mapping for forbidding forbidden punctuation at line start/end. Declared in .cjk-strict. Exact codepoint coverage is engine-dependent; not pixel-verified.

rules.clreqLocator: §6.1.1 (prohibition-rules-basic): 'Opening quotation marks, opening parentheses, and opening angle brackets should not appear at the line end.'
rules.note: Same CSS mechanism; opening brackets kept off line end.

rules.clreqLocator: §6.1.1 (prohibition-rules-strict): 'two-em dashes and ellipses should not appear at the line start' (additive over GB-style)
rules.note: CSS line-break: strict covers the strict set where the engine supports it; not pixel-verified.

rules.clreqLocator: §6.1.1 (prohibition-rules-none): 'Ignore all prohibition against line breaks. Commonly used in newspapers in Taiwan and Hong Kong.'
rules.note: Rendered as the .cjk-loose comparison paragraph. Demonstrates the 'none' end of CLREQ's four strictness levels.

rules.clreqLocator: §6.1 Line breaking & hyphenation (general CJK line breaking between Han characters)
rules.note: Standard CJK line-breaking control; declared explicitly to avoid break-all.

rules.clreqLocator: §6.1.2 Prohibition rules for unbreakable marks (符号分离禁则): 'certain punctuation marks ... take up 2 em of space. They should not be broken across two lines.' (e.g. two-em dash / ellipsis pairs)
rules.note: No faithful CSS-only mechanism keeps a specific 2-em punctuation unit unbroken across lines in all engines; would need engine-level line breaking or JS measurement. NOT asserted.

rules.clreqLocator: §6.3.2 Punctuation Width Adjustment / compression of adjacent punctuation marks (标点挤压); §6.1.1 notes compression MUST be processed BEFORE prohibition rules
rules.note: Punctuation compression/挤压 has no interoperable CSS equivalent; text-spacing-trim is not broadly supported. NOT asserted.

rules.clreqLocator: §6.1.3 Hanging punctuation at line end (行尾点号悬挂): 'Most Chinese publications do not use hanging punctuation at line end'; only certain pause/stop marks may overhang
rules.cssProperty: hanging-punctuation: allow-end (limited support; deliberately NOT applied)
rules.note: CLREQ itself says most Chinese publications do NOT use hanging punctuation; support is limited and locale-dependent. Left unimplemented/untested rather than faking compliance.

rules.clreqLocator: §6.2.2 Line adjustment / reduction and expansion of inter-character spacing (挤压与拉伸/均排), §6.3.1.2 Even inter-character spacing
rules.note: CSS text-align:justify is NOT equivalent to CLREQ's priority-ordered inter-character reduction/expansion + '先挤进，后推出'. NOT asserted.

rules.clreqLocator: §6.1.4 / §6.2.1: Han-Western mixed text spacing; 'the spacing made available during line adjustment processing'
rules.note: Automatic Han/Western spacing is not interoperably supported in the test engine; NOT asserted.
